요구가 둘입니다. ① 지금 DB를 내린다(stop). ② 작업 중에 올라: There are two requirements. ① Shut down the DB now (stop). ② Keep it from coming up during the work (disable). They are different commands.
지금 상태를 자세히 기록하기: Record the current state in detail
두 인스턴스 모두 Open입니다. 작업 전 상태를 남겨 두어야 작업 뒤에: Both instances are Open. You must record the state before the work to compare afterwards "whether it came back as it was" (field guide: re-verify with the same commands before and after the work).
리포트 서비스부터 세션을 비우며 내리기 (drain): Shut down the report service first while draining sessions (drain)
<code>-drain_timeout 60</code>은 새 접속은 막고: -drain_timeout 60 means new connections are blocked and attached sessions are given up to 60 seconds to finish their work and leave. The planned work example in High Availability Overview 19c uses -drain_timeout and -stopoption together like this. Sessions still left after the time are cleaned up with the -stopoption method. For -wait, that document has only one line, "in scripts it helps to include wait = yes", and the option's description could not be confirmed.
PAYDB 전체를 정상 종료하기: Shut down all of PAYDB cleanly
한 명령으로 두 인스턴스가 함께 내려갑니다. -stopoption 값은: One command takes both instances down together. -stopoption values are NORMAL, TRANSACTIONAL, IMMEDIATE, and ABORT (RAC 19c option table). Compared with typing SHUTDOWN in SQL*Plus on each node, there is less risk of missing one, and Clusterware records it as "shut down on purpose".
두 인스턴스 모두 not running입니다(이 문구는 19c 예시로 확: Both instances are not running (this wording could not be confirmed with a 19c example).
작업 중에 올라오지 않게 disable 하기: Disable it so it doesn't come up during the work
RAC 19c: srvctl disable database는 DB를 비활: RAC 19c: srvctl disable database disables the DB, and "if the database is a cluster database, its instances are also disabled." disable is not stop. It does not turn off what is running; it only changes the flag so Clusterware does not start or manage this resource. So the order is stop, then disable. Now even if the server reboots, PAYDB will not come up.
Clusterware 쪽에서도 확인하기: Also check from the Clusterware side
<code>ora.paydb.db</code>의 Target이 OFFLI: The Target of ora.paydb.db is OFFLINE, and config shows Database is disabled. The names and order of the config lines follow the srvctl config database example in the RAC 19c documentation; the enabled/disabled line is not in the documentation example and could not be confirmed.
작업이 끝났다고 가정하고 enable 후 DB 올리기: Assume the work is done, enable, and start the DB
enable을 빼고 start를 하면 이 실습은 disable 상태라 시: If you start without enable, this lab tells you it cannot start because it is disabled. Without -startoption, it opens with the default OPEN (RAC 19c: "the default is OPEN"). If you need to inspect it, you can bring it up only to mount with -startoption MOUNT.
서비스 상태 보고 리포트 서비스 다시 시작하기: View the service status and restart the report service
pay_oltp, pay_batch는 DB와 함께 올라왔지만 pay_re: pay_oltp and pay_batch came up with the DB, but pay_report is not running, because it is a service we stopped separately with srvctl stop service. What was stopped on purpose must be restarted on purpose.
echo '22:00 스토리지 작업: pay_report drain 중지: echo '22:00 storage work: pay_report drain stop -> stop database immediate -> disable database. After work: enable -> start database -> pay_report start. status -detail same as before work' > ~/storage_maint.txt
이 레슨을 마쳤습니다. Start/Stop은 \"지금 실행 상태\"를,: You have finished this lesson. Start/Stop changes "the current running state", and Enable/Disable changes "whether Clusterware may start and manage it" (the distinction in the field guide). Using the two as a pair is the key.
srvctl은 같은 DB나 서비스에 여러 명령을 동시에 실행하는 것을 지: srvctl does not support running several commands at the same time on the same DB or service (RAC 19c: "SRVCTL does not support concurrent executions of commands on the same object"). Assign a single operator so that two people don't handle the same DB from different terminals. Also, if you want to see what will change before actually running it, the -eval option lets you "simulate without changing anything" (RAC 19c: supported for start/stop database, start/stop/relocate service, and others).
패치 리허설: 세션 비우고 홈 단위로 내렸다 올리기: Patch rehearsal: drain sessions and stop and restart by home
\"다음 주에 racnode2 DB 홈에 RU를 적용합니다. 오늘은 리허: "Next week we apply an RU to the racnode2 DB home. Today is a rehearsal. First empty the settlement batch to PAYDB1, stop only what runs from that home on racnode2, and then bring it back exactly as it was before stopping." The plan is in ~/work_request.txt.
패치는 홈 단위로 합니다(8단계). racnode2의 DB 홈을 고치는: Patching is done by home (stage 8). While the DB home on racnode2 is being fixed, PAYDB1 on racnode1 keeps working. This is the basic shape of "rolling patching", RAC's biggest advantage.
pay_batch runs only on PAYDB2. Empty this first.
세션에 2분 여유를 주고 pay_batch 옮기기: Move pay_batch, giving sessions 2 minutes of grace
High Availability Overview 19c에는 relocat: High Availability Overview 19c has a form of relocate service with -drain_timeout and -stopoption. Unlike cutting sessions right away with -force, it gives working sessions time to finish and then moves. The field guide also says relocate changes "only the current running location, temporarily", and to change the preferred and available settings permanently, use srvctl modify service.
racnode2의 DB 홈에서 도는 자원을 상태 파일과 함께 멈추기: Stop the resources running from the DB home on racnode2, with a state file
<code>stop home</code>은 그 노드에서 이 홈으로 도는: stop home stops all resources running from this home on that node (the PAYDB2 instance and the services on it) at once, and writes to a state file what was running before the stop. RAC 19c option table: -statefile is "the path to the state_file created by a previously executed srvctl stop home". The full syntax of stop home and start home could not be confirmed in the 19c documentation; it follows the field guide.
멈추기 전 PAYDB2에서 돌던 DB와 서비스가 적혀 있습니다. 파일 안: It lists the DB and services that were running on PAYDB2 before the stop. The layout inside the file was made up for this lab. The important point is that start home needs this file to bring back exactly "only what was running". So if you keep it in /tmp, you must use it before a reboot wipes it, and in the field it is sometimes kept in a location that won't be wiped.
PAYDB1만 일하는지 확인하기: Check that only PAYDB1 is working
PAYDB2는 not running, 서비스는 모두 PAYDB1에서 돕니: PAYDB2 is not running, and all services run on PAYDB1. In reality, this is where you patch the racnode2 DB home with OPatch (the part you practiced in stage 8).
패치가 끝났다고 가정하고 같은 상태 파일로 되살리기: Assume the patch is done and bring it back with the same state file
실무 가이드: stop home이 기록한 상태 파일을 start home: Field guide: using the state file recorded by stop home with start home brings back the resources that were running from that home before the work. PAYDB2 came back, along with pay_oltp, which was running on PAYDB2 before the stop.
서비스 확인하고 pay_batch 되돌리기: Check the services and restore pay_batch
pay_batch는 stop home보다 먼저 우리가 직접 옮긴 것이라: pay_batch was moved by us before stop home, so it was not in the state file. That is why it does not come back with start home and must be restored by hand. It is why a record of "who moved what, and when" is needed.
echo 'racnode2 홈 패치 리허설: pay_batch drain: echo 'racnode2 home patch rehearsal: moved pay_batch to PAYDB1 with 120s drain, stop home (statefile /tmp/dbhome_racnode2.state), start home restored PAYDB2 and pay_oltp, pay_batch restored by hand. In the real work, OPatch goes after stop home' > ~/patch_rehearsal.txt
You have finished this lesson. Next is the stage 11 graduation mission.
세션 drain은 \"끊지 않고 비우는\" 기술입니다. 서비스를 옮기거나: Session drain is a technique for "emptying without cutting". When moving or stopping a service with -drain_timeout, apps using a connection pool (UCP and others) receive a FAN notification, close idle connections first, and open new connections to another instance. High Availability Overview 19c shows examples of emptying services like this during planned work before stopping the instance. If the app cannot receive notifications, sessions are cut by the -stopoption method after the drain time, so decide the time value with the app owner.
졸업 미션: 노드 장애 뒤 서비스 되돌리기: Graduation mission: restore services after a node failure
\"오늘 아침 정산 배치가 평소보다 두 배 느려요. 결제 화면도 조금 느: "This morning's settlement batch is twice as slow as usual. People also say the payment screen is a bit slow." Overnight log: "03:10 racnode2 server rebooted after a hardware alarm, 07:40 confirmed normal startup (infrastructure team)". Find the cause, set it right, and report in ~/rac_incident.txt.
클러스터와 자원 상태부터 보기: Start with the cluster and resource status
두 노드 모두 online이고 PAYDB1, PAYDB2도 Open입니다: Both nodes are online, and PAYDB1 and PAYDB2 are Open. When the server came back on, Clusterware restarted the instance. But ora.paydb.pay_batch.svc is on racnode1, not its usual place (racnode2).
pay_batch가 PAYDB1에서 돌고 있습니다. racnode2가 내: pay_batch is running on PAYDB1. When racnode2 went down, the preferred instance (PAYDB2) disappeared, so it moved to the available one (PAYDB1), and it stayed there even after racnode2 came back. RAC Administration Guide 19c (services): "Oracle does not automatically relocate a service back to a preferred instance when the preferred instance restarts." As the reason, the documentation says the service is already running on the desired number of instances, and relocating it back would cause a second interruption. Same document: from 19.3, setting a service's -failback attribute to yes makes it go back to the preferred instance when that instance comes back.
SQL로 인스턴스별·서비스별 세션 수 보기: View session counts per instance and service with SQL
PAYDB1(INST_ID 1)에 pay_oltp 8개와 pay_batc: On PAYDB1 (INST_ID 1), 8 pay_oltp sessions and 12 pay_batch sessions are attached together, while PAYDB2 has only pay_oltp. The payment screens and the settlement batch are competing on one server. That is why "the batch is slow and the screens are slow too".
배치 세션이 무엇을 기다리는지 보기: See what the batch sessions are waiting for
<code>gc cr block 2-way</code>, <code>gc: Waits starting with gc, such as gc cr block 2-way and gc current block 2-way, are global cache waits. RAC Administration Guide 19c (performance monitoring): it lists gc current block 2-way, gc cr block 2-way, and others as key block-related waits, and groups such waits into the Cluster wait class. It is waiting while blocks held by another instance are passed back and forth. The session counts and wait ratios are example values for this lab. Splitting payments and the batch by instance reduces how often the two instances pass the same blocks back and forth.
pay_batch를 원래 자리(PAYDB2)로 되돌리기: Move pay_batch back to its usual place (PAYDB2)
출력이 없으면 성공입니다. -force 없이 옮겼으므로 지금 돌고 있는: No output means success. It was moved without -force, so the batch sessions running now were not cut. Batch jobs starting from now connect to PAYDB2. Whether the current batch can be cut must be decided with the settlement team, so don't clean up the server on your own.
서비스와 자원 상태를 다시 확인하기: Check the service and resource status again
pay_batch는 PAYDB2, pay_oltp는 두 인스턴스에서 돕니: pay_batch runs on PAYDB2, and pay_oltp on both instances. It is back to its usual shape.
echo '03:10 racnode2 재부팅으로 pay_batch가 PA: echo '03:10 racnode2 reboot moved pay_batch PAYDB2->PAYDB1 (available). Did not return automatically after racnode2 came back at 07:40 -> payments and batch piled on PAYDB1, causing delays. Restored to PAYDB2 with srvctl relocate service, running batch sessions kept. Prevention: add service location check after node recovery to checklist, consider -failback option' > ~/rac_incident.txt
수고했습니다. 11단계 RAC 기초를 마쳤습니다. 클러스터 점검(olsn: Good work. You have finished stage 11, RAC basics. You have done cluster checks (olsnodes, crsctl), DB and service management (srvctl), and whole-RAC views (GV$) once each, and you have experienced firsthand the field trap that "the service may stay put even after the node comes back".
RAC 장애는 \"서버가 죽었다\"보다 \"죽었다 살아난 뒤의 상태가 평: RAC incidents show up more often as "the state after it died and came back differs from normal" than as "the server died". Be sure to put service locations, SCAN listener locations, and the instance where sessions piled up on the checklist after a node recovers. Moving a service is easy in itself, but when to move it must be decided with the business owner. Cutting sessions with -force may mean an in-progress batch has to run again from the start.
